title: Reflection, rotation and rotational symmetry
summary: Plot points in all four quadrants, reflect shapes in an axis, rotate them about a point, and find shapes with a centre of symmetry.
guide: Extending both axes past 0 splits the grid into four {{term:quadrant}}s. A negative x-coordinate is left of the origin; a negative y-coordinate is below it. (−3, 2) means 3 left, then 2 up.

A {{term:reflection}} works like a mirror: every point ends up the same distance away on the other side of the mirror line. Reflecting in the y-axis changes the sign of x and keeps y. The classic slip is sliding the shape across instead of flipping it.

In a {{term:rotation}} the shape turns about a point, the centre of rotation. For 90°, turn the line from the centre to each vertex through a quarter turn. Tracing paper with a pencil point on the centre helps a lot. (Rotation is not in the KS2 curriculum; treat it as enrichment.)

A shape that fits onto itself after a half turn has {{term:rotational-symmetry}} of order 2 (also called {{term:point-symmetry}}), and the point it turns about is its centre of symmetry: parallelograms and rectangles are examples. An equilateral triangle fits onto itself after a third of a turn (order 3), but not after a half turn.

engine.letters: A B C D E F G H I J
engine.instruction-mirror: Draw the reflection, then tap the first vertex again.
engine.instruction-tap: Tap the shapes with a centre of symmetry.

four-quadrants.title: Four quadrants
four-quadrants.prompt: Plot the point A{{vec:-3,2}}. Which quadrant is it in?
four-quadrants.hint: x is −3: go 3 to the left of the origin. y is 2: then go 2 up.
four-quadrants.success: Well done! A(−3, 2) is in the second quadrant: left of the y-axis and above the x-axis.
four-quadrants.why: Where is (3, 2)? How is it related to A?
four-quadrants.model: (3, 2) is in the first quadrant, 3 to the right of the origin. The two points are reflections of each other in the y-axis: same y-coordinate, opposite x-coordinates.

feedback.empty: Tap the grid to plot a point.
feedback.sign: You left out the minus sign. x = −3 means 3 to the left of the origin, not the right.
feedback.sign-y: x is right, but y = 2 is positive: the point is above the x-axis.
feedback.swapped: You swapped x and y. The first number (−3) is across.
feedback.too-many: Plot just one point. Tap a point again to remove it.
feedback.wrong-point: That point is not (−3, 2). From the origin go 3 left, then 2 up.

reflect-y-axis.title: Reflect in the y-axis
reflect-y-axis.prompt: Reflect triangle ABC in the y-axis (the dashed line). Predict first: where will the image of B{{vec:4,1}} be?
reflect-y-axis.hint: Each vertex goes the same distance to the other side of the mirror line. B is 4 to the right of the axis, so its image is 4 to the left, at the same height.
reflect-y-axis.success: Well done! That is the reflection. The triangle has flipped over, like a mirror image.
reflect-y-axis.why: Compare the coordinates of each vertex and its image. What changed, and what stayed the same?
reflect-y-axis.model: The x-coordinates changed sign and the y-coordinates stayed the same: A(1, 1) went to (−1, 1) and B(4, 1) went to (−4, 1). Reflecting in the y-axis only swaps left and right.

feedback.empty: Tap the grid to draw the reflection.
feedback.open: Your shape is still open. Tap the first vertex to close it.
feedback.slid: You slid the same triangle across. A reflection flips it: B, the vertex furthest from the axis, must be furthest on the other side too.
feedback.not-image: That is not the reflection. Count how far each vertex is from the dashed line and go the same distance on the other side, at the same height.

rotate-quarter.title: Rotate 90°
rotate-quarter.prompt: Rotate triangle ABC 90° clockwise about the origin, and draw its image.
rotate-quarter.hint: Turn the line from the origin to each vertex a quarter turn clockwise. C(1, 4) is above the origin; after the turn it is to the right: (4, −1).
rotate-quarter.success: Well done! The triangle made a quarter turn clockwise, from the first quadrant to the fourth.
rotate-quarter.why: Look at A(1, 1) and its image. Can you find a rule for this rotation?
rotate-quarter.model: A(1, 1) went to (1, −1), B(3, 1) to (1, −3) and C(1, 4) to (4, −1). The old y-coordinate becomes the new x, and the old x with its sign changed becomes the new y: (x, y) → (y, −x).

feedback.empty: Tap the grid to draw the image.
feedback.open: Your shape is still open. Tap the first vertex to close it.
feedback.wrong-way: You turned it anticlockwise, into the second quadrant. Clockwise turns up towards the right.
feedback.not-image: That is not the rotated triangle. Turn each vertex on its own: C(1, 4) goes to (4, −1). Each vertex must stay the same distance from the origin.

centre-of-symmetry.title: Centre of symmetry
centre-of-symmetry.prompt: Which shapes look exactly the same after a half turn about their middle? Tap all of them.
centre-of-symmetry.hint: Imagine turning each shape upside down. Is it the same shape? In a shape with a centre of symmetry, every vertex has a partner straight across the middle.
centre-of-symmetry.success: Well done! The parallelogram, the blue shape and the rectangle all have a centre of symmetry.
centre-of-symmetry.why: The equilateral triangle fits onto itself after a third of a turn. So why did it not count?
centre-of-symmetry.model: We wanted shapes that fit after a half turn. Turn the triangle half a turn and its point is at the bottom, so it does not fit. It has rotational symmetry of order 3, but not of order 2.

feedback.empty: Tap the shapes that look the same after a half turn.
feedback.third-turn: The green triangle fits onto itself after a third of a turn, but a half turn leaves it upside down. It has no centre of symmetry.
feedback.line-only: That shape has a line of symmetry, but no centre of symmetry. Turn it half a turn: its top and bottom are different.
feedback.extra: One shape you tapped does not fit onto itself after a half turn. Tap it again to remove it.
feedback.missed: There is another shape that fits onto itself after a half turn.

complete-half-turn.title: Complete the shape
complete-half-turn.prompt: The red dot is the centre of symmetry. Draw the other half. Start at the red dot; the line ends after 4 points.
complete-half-turn.hint: In a half turn every point goes the same distance to the other side of the centre. A vertex 2 squares above the centre goes to 2 squares below it.
complete-half-turn.success: Well done! The shape now looks the same after a half turn about the red dot.
complete-half-turn.why: Where does the vertex at (7, 5) go when it is turned about the centre (4, 4)? How do you know?
complete-half-turn.model: To (1, 3). From the centre to (7, 5) is 3 right and 1 up, so its image is 3 left and 1 down from the centre. The centre is the midpoint of each point and its image.

feedback.empty: Start at the red dot and draw the other half.
feedback.not-image: That half is not a half turn. Did you reflect it in a line? A half turn sends up to down and right to left, both at once.
